recordDecisions.title: An independent counting-hierarchy proof for real feasibility with a fourth-level bound
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Meiburg reports existential real feasibility in BPP^(C3P), hence C4P, and for fixed w alternating real quantifier blocks a C(9w+17)P upper bound. The paper gives additional explicitly modeled bounds for exact SDP, PosSLP and square-root sum. This is an independent proof package and a stronger reported level bound than OpenAI3730, not a second first-public settlement of the general CH containment.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The primary paper says ChatGPT discovered the proofs during conversations ending September29 and wrote essentially all mathematical content; Meiburg reports no nontrivial mathematical development role and an ongoing human digestion/exposition effort. Exact model is not disclosed.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Audit uniform bit-access and counting-oracle levels, randomized sign reconstruction, singular critical fibers and the input encodings/promises for each application. Independently compare the C4 bound with OpenAI3730's constituent manuscript and prior real-algebraic complexity work. September29 is an author-reported completion date, not established public visibility; first arXiv submission is October7. Human researchers had not completed the full proof digestion. Do not infer PSPACE=CH, deterministic C3 membership or a universal claim about every application. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: A new stronger level bound and independently generated proof after an earlier public general-containment claim, rather than a second first settlement of the long-standing general target.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: First arXiv submission; manuscript completion dates do not establish prior public visibility.

recordDecisions.title: A conditional nonsmooth hot-spots extension for simple first eigenvalues
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Assuming the explicitly stated smooth-domain no-critical-point theorem, Burdzy reports non-strict boundary-layer supremum/infimum equalities for first positive Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded simply connected planar domains with compact Neumann resolvent and simple first positive eigenvalue, without boundary smoothness. Boundary maximum/minimum equalities follow when the eigenfunction extends continuously to the closure. Spectral convergence is proved separately without the smooth-domain input.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Burdzy says ChatGPT generated the note from multiple human prompts. He had not checked every detail, regards it as an obvious human-accessible corollary, and reports an almost identical simultaneous ChatGPT proof by Rodrigo Bañuelos, requesting equal credit rather than sole priority.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Keep the smooth-domain assertion as an explicit unverified external premise, not verification or unconditional extension of OpenAI3955. Audit conformal exhaustion, weighted square-integrability and spectral convergence. Retain compact resolvent, simplicity and non-strict conclusion; no assertion of a nonvanishing gradient or continuous boundary values for all rough domains. Resolve simultaneous credit and novelty without counting the unavailable Bañuelos note separately. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: The author explicitly describes the conditional approximation argument as an obvious corollary that humans can readily prove; not another settlement of the original hot-spots frontier.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: First arXiv submission; manuscript completion dates do not establish prior public visibility.

recordDecisions.title: Inverse resonance uniqueness and finite-data estimates with a complex Robin boundary condition
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Shterenberg reports a complex-Robin analogue of the Marletta–Shterenberg–Weikard half-line inverse-resonance method for complex L1 potentials supported in [0,1]. For a fixed known complex Robin parameter, the full zero set of the Robin characteristic function with multiplicities determines the potential; finite-data characteristic-function and potential estimates hold under the paper's stated bounds and integrability hypotheses. Constants can be uniform on bounded parameter sets; the boundary parameter is not jointly reconstructed.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The primary paper says the text was produced with help from ChatGPT for Academy. It does not identify mathematical discovery, retained theorem-level steps, exact model or a division between prose and substantive assistance.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Establish whether the explicit AI acknowledgement covers mathematical work rather than only writing; compare novelty with earlier Robin inverse-resonance literature. Audit high-energy normalization, Hadamard factors, boundary trace recovery, zero multiplicities and additional hypotheses of the quantitative estimates. Do not replace a fixed known a by joint recovery of a and q, or identify zeros in z with unsigned energy eigenvalues. Independent proof review is not established. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: A specialist extension of an existing transformation-operator method, not a claimed resolution of a long-standing barrier.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: First arXiv submission; manuscript completion dates do not establish prior public visibility.

recordDecisions.title: Sharp quartic Lyapunov boundaries and sextic degree separation for a planar cubic family
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Jones reports that for the displayed planar cubic field f_b=(-R+b(x²-y²))(x,y)+R(-y,x), R=x²+y², positive real homogeneous quartic Lyapunov certificates exist strictly exactly when |b|<B and weakly exactly when |b|<=B, B approximately2.128153533. At b=B the full cone of quartics with nonpositive derivative is one nonnegative ray. Integer certificates separate degrees2/4 at b=2 and4/6 at b=9/4. The all-degree variable-damping criterion is a written supplement, not part of the compared Lean endpoint.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Owner disclosure credits human-directed GPT6/GPT6 Astra via Codex/ChatGPT with mathematical arguments, exact certificate discovery, formal proofs and checking, with the underlying field and obstruction methods attributed to Liu–Fitzsimmons.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check the unrestricted real-coefficient quartic quantifiers, boundary polynomial/root isolation, derivative semantics and endpoint cone. Audit degree-separation identities independently; do not promote the written all-degree and damping supplements into verified formal coverage. Establish novelty against Liu–Fitzsimmons and other polynomial Lyapunov degree obstructions. No exact sextic feasibility boundary or independently reviewed ODE stability theorem is claimed. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: Exact finite-degree feasibility and obstruction classification for a fixed vector-field family, not general automated stability or all-degree solution.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary registration; earlier repository/paper visibility remains an explicit unresolved date question.

recordDecisions.title: Exact real dimension-three and complex dimension-two Recht–Ré counterexamples
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Jones reports five real symmetric PSD3x3 integer matrices and five complex Hermitian PSD2x2 Gaussian-integer matrices, each tuple summing to100I, whose norm-of-averaged-product ratio at n=k=5 is10329/10000>1. These lower the real dimension of De Sa's explicit dimension-five benchmark; complex dimension two is minimal by scalar AM–GM. The unrestricted real symmetric2x2 case remains unresolved. The already-known universal disproof is not a new settlement here.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Primary disclosure credits OpenAI GPT, Claude and Grok with research, computation, writing and formalization; OpenAI GPT prepared the final manuscript and formalization. De Sa's dimension-five matrices and19/16 ratio are explicitly reused background, not attributed to this AI discovery.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently check PSD Gram factors, all120 ordered products, Euclidean operator norm and exact ratio. Complete a low-dimensional prior-art check; the owner's search is explicitly non-exhaustive. Separate two formal existential witnesses from written parameter-family/optimization and positive-definite extensions. Do not assert real2x2 impossibility, a palindromic variant, global optimality or a new disproof of the2012 universal conjecture. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: A concrete low-dimensional construction improving a known explicit benchmark, not the first universal counterexample.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary registration; earlier repository/paper visibility remains an explicit unresolved date question.

recordDecisions.title: A strengthened asymptotic two-eigenvalue bound for forbidden subgraphs
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Shaik reports that for every fixed finite F with chromatic number r+1>=3 and every epsilon>0, all sufficiently large-edge finite simple F-free graphs satisfy F2(A)<=2(1-1/r)m-(2(1-1/r)-1)Delta+epsilon m. F2 sums the squares of the two largest positive adjacency eigenvalues, padding zeros. A companion proves eventual equality with the two largest ordered eigenvalue squares. Disconnected graphs are allowed; no explicit effective threshold is supplied.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Pinned owner metadata attributes AI-assisted formalization and package extraction to GPT6 Codex, reusing Shengtong Zhang's BN Gram and nonedge-interlacing developments and attributed Mathlib regularity infrastructure. The exact origin of the new informal argument is not independently established.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: The informal source is a private manuscript and cannot be read independently. Audit weighted removal, hub separation, uniformity in graph size, maximum-degree penalty and eventual ordered-eigenvalue correspondence. Establish novelty/material AI argument allocation beyond inherited BN support; no blanket verification promotion of1308,4017 or4018. This asymptotic claim is distinct from the exact bounds refuted by4017 and the localized claim4018. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: Substantial asymptotic spectral extremal progress with a stated degree penalty; distinct from an exact counterexample or a second proof of the inherited BN theorem.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary registration; earlier repository/paper visibility remains an explicit unresolved date question.

recordDecisions.title: A converse to the discrete four-vertex theorem and realization continuity
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Josefsson reports a solution of Tabachnikov's2007 Problem2: every admissible cyclic positive radius sequence with at least two distinct plateau maxima and minima, for every n>=4, is realized by a simple strictly convex coherent polygon. The paper gives the corresponding side-tangent characterization, local C1 choices near nonconstant data and an explicit hexagon obstruction to a global continuous realization choice. These are original results developed with the formalization, not only Dahlberg's established forward theorem.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Owner metadata says the mathematics and proofs were developed with Aristotle, Claude, Codex and DeepSeek assistance. It names Claude Opus4.8/Fable5/Opus5.5 through Claude Code/Archon and an Aristotle prover loop; the author takes responsibility and says paper and formalization were developed together.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Verify correspondence to Tabachnikov's exact Problem2 and the plateau convention, all-n realization and coherent-convex geometry. Check the signed-Menger-curvature regular-hexagon formulation underlying the global obstruction and the local C1 hypotheses; audit side-tangent endpoints separately. Establish earliest public paper visibility and later-prior-art history. Owner/compiler/comparator statements are not independent human proof review or replay here; forward classical theorems are not extra new records. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: Reported complete solution for every n>=4 of the exact discrete realization problem posed by Tabachnikov in2007, rather than the already-known forward four-vertex theorem.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary registration; earlier repository/paper visibility remains an explicit unresolved date question.

recordDecisions.title: An explicit Hausdorff waist bound and repaired spherical localization argument
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Akopyan's package reports that for every continuous map S^n to R^k with1<=k<=n, some fiber has Mathlib unnormalized chordal (n-k)-dimensional Hausdorff measure at least1/(12*4^n*3^k), via a modification of Klartag's localization. It also reports repairing a discontinuous center-selection step in Memarian's spherical proof by cap quasiconcavity and continuous selection. The other headline waist theorems are established mathematics; the sharp intermediate-dimensional Hausdorff constant remains open.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: Primary metadata says Arseniy Akopyan prepared the formalization with Aristotle over several weeks. It does not establish whether Aristotle originated the explicit bound or gap repair, or only translated human mathematical modifications.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Establish novelty/materiality of the explicit positive bound and repaired proof route, as distinct from known waist formalizations. Audit spherical versus chordal metric, unnormalized Hausdorff measure and conversion factor omega_d/2^d, fiber quantifiers and selection continuity. Do not claim the sharp Gromov Hausdorff conjecture, or count all nine classical endpoints as new discoveries. Exact human/AI allocation and independent proof/statement replay remain unresolved. No downloaded proof artifact was executed. Keep provisional=1, low strict confidence, taxonomy unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
recordDecisions.comparator: A bounded quantitative fiber estimate and source-reported repair within classical waist theory, not a claimed sharp solution of Gromov's conjecture.
recordDecisions.dateBasis: Earliest supported dated primary registration; earlier repository/paper visibility remains an explicit unresolved date question.
